title: Cantilever column: first and second elastic critical load

source.work: McGuire, W., Gallagher, R. H., Ziemian, R. D., Matrix Structural Analysis
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited pages; nothing of the source is reproduced

analysis: Plane (x-y) problem of the source modelled in 3D with the global Y axis vertical, so that the source's x, y and theta_z are the model's X, Y and rz. In-plane bending is about local z for every member (default orientation), hence the source's I is the section's Iz. Column of 10 m, A = 7.2e3 mm^2, I = 150e6 mm^4, E = 200,000 MPa, base fixed, top free. Reference load 1 kN downward at the top. Linear buckling analysis, one member, two modes. Targets: the theoretical values the source prints for comparison, pi^2 EI/(4 L^2) = 740 kN and 9 pi^2 EI/(4 L^2) = 6662 kN. The engine's members carry the exact stability functions (no discretisation error for a prismatic member with constant axial force); the source's computed values use a stated number of elements with a polynomial (approximate) geometric stiffness. The source's one-element results (746 kN, stated to be within 1.5 %, and 9651 kN) and its two-element second mode (6884 kN, within 3.3 %) are its own approximations and are not targets. Plane stability problem: the source's model has no out-of-plane degrees of freedom. Here the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held and Iy = 1000 Iz, so that no out-of-plane buckling mode precedes the in-plane modes compared; J is a placeholder.
